title: Gangplank OIDC login broken for all personas: invalid_client / token_endpoint_auth_method mismatch
description: https://gangplank.<ip>.sslip.io/ Sign in redirects through Authelia OIDC and then bounces to /callback with error=invalid_target, and the page body shows: oauth2: "invalid_client" "Client authentication failed ... The request was determined to be using 'token_endpoint_auth_method' method 'client_secret_post', however the OAuth 2.0 client registration does not allow this method." Reproduced live via Playwright browser flow — this blocks K8s kubeconfig dispensing for every persona (admin, rbr-admin, rbr-ver-admin, rbr-ver-dev, rbr-po, unrelated), i.e. the entire K8s/Capsule column of the persona-access matrix in docs/plan-tenant-personas-authelia.md is currently unverifiable end-to-end and likely nonfunctional for real users. Root cause is a mismatch between the token_endpoint_auth_method the gangplank client actually uses (client_secret_post) and what Authelia's OIDC client registration for gangplank allows (see gangplank client definition in authelia/config/configuration.yaml.tpl) — likely needs an explicit token_endpoint_auth_method: 'client_secret_post' (or client_secret_basic, matching whatever gangplank actually sends) added to that client stanza. Highest priority of the persona-matrix findings since it blocks an entire consumer, not just specific personas.

title: SeaweedFS weed mini S3 health check fails: -s3.port=0 probes http://ip:0 (disabled port)
description: weed mini health check probes the HTTP S3 port after startup. When -s3.port=0 (HTTP disabled), it probes http://ip:0 which always fails, marking S3 as 'failed'. This destabilizes the HTTPS S3 listener on 8333 and causes TLS handshake timeouts from Loki/bucket-init. Fix: use -s3.port=8334 (HTTP +1) instead of 0, so health check has a valid HTTP endpoint to probe, while HTTPS stays on 8333.
notes: Root cause: weed mini -s3.port=0 causes health check to probe http://ip:0 (disabled port), marking S3 'failed'. Additionally, weed mini may not correctly initialize the TLS listener via CLI flags. Fix: (1) switch from 'weed mini' to 'weed server -filer -s3' — the primary tested code path for S3 TLS; (2) use -s3.port=8334 (HTTP +1) instead of 0, so a valid HTTP endpoint exists; (3) explicitly set -volume.port=9340 since weed server defaults to 8080 not 9340. Files: scripts/common.sh (add SEAWEEDFS_S3_HTTP_PORT=8334, remove SEAWEEDFS_ADMIN_PORT), scripts/setup.sh (both initial run and TLS restart updated).
close_reason: Fixed: switched from 'weed mini' to 'weed server -filer -s3'. HTTP port moved to 8334, volume.port=9340 made explicit, SEAWEEDFS_S3_HTTP_PORT added to common.sh.

title: In-cluster forward-auth 400: Traefik strips X-Forwarded-Method to edge Authelia
description: In-cluster services behind Authelia forward-auth (e.g. radar.172-18-255-200.sslip.io) returned a bare 400 Bad Request instead of the login portal. Authelia (now edge-only, reached cross-boundary via the authelia-backend ExternalName) logged: Error getting Target URL and Request Method, error="header 'X-Forwarded-Method' is empty". Root cause: Traefik strips incoming X-Forwarded-* (incl. X-Forwarded-Method) from untrusted sources unless entryPoints.<name>.forwardedHeaders.trustedIPs is set; no such trust was configured, so both the in-cluster and edge Traefik hops relaying the forwardAuth sub-request dropped the header. Fix: forwardedHeaders.trustedIPs=[172.18.0.0/16,10.244.0.0/16] on the websecure entrypoint of both Traefik instances (traefik/values.yaml additionalArguments + traefik-edge/traefik.yaml). Verified: radar now 302-redirects to the Authelia Sign in page.
close_reason: Fixed: added forwardedHeaders.trustedIPs (172.18.0.0/16,10.244.0.0/16) to websecure on both in-cluster (helm upgrade) and edge (container restart) Traefik. Verified radar 302->Authelia login portal; Authelia now parses method=GET.

title: Edge OTLP export fails: collector server cert has no IP SAN for LB IP 172.18.255.240
description: The external edge Traefik dials the OTel collector by LB IP (172.18.255.240:4317) with mTLS. The collector server cert (Certificate otel-collector-otlp-tls in monitoring/platform/ext-svc-lb.yaml) only had DNS SANs, so Go's gRPC TLS client rejected the handshake: 'x509: cannot validate certificate for 172.18.255.240 because it doesn't contain any IP SANs'. Result: ALL edge OTLP export (traces AND logs AND access logs) failed silently — this blocked xcl validation. openssl s_client verify=0 was misleading (openssl does not enforce IP-SAN matching by default; Go does). Fix: added ipAddresses: [172.18.255.240] to the Certificate; cert-manager reissued; collector rolled out. Verified: edge traces+logs now land as service_name/resource.service.name=traefik-edge in Tempo and Loki with zero export errors.
close_reason: Fixed: added IP SAN 172.18.255.240 to otel-collector-otlp-tls Certificate (monitoring/platform/ext-svc-lb.yaml); cert reissued, collector restarted; edge OTLP handshake now succeeds, verified traefik-edge telemetry in Tempo+Loki.

title: authelia container ends up on bridge network only, not kind → edge Traefik 504 to authelia, all Authelia SSO down
description:
REGRESSION found during 5sq MCP verification (2026-07-02, clean recreate).

SYMPTOM: traefik-edge returns HTTP 504 for every path to the authelia backend (edge portal authelia.172-18-0-250.sslip.io AND in-cluster portal authelia.172-18-255-200.sslip.io, which proxies to the edge via the authelia-backend ExternalName). Cascades: seaweedfs-admin forward-auth middleware -> 500; grafana/argocd/tenant-grafana OAuth/OIDC logins cannot complete.

ROOT CAUSE: the 'authelia' host container is attached to the docker 'bridge' network only (172.17.0.4), NOT the 'kind' network. traefik-edge is on 'kind' only (172.18.0.250), so it cannot reach 'authelia:9091'. By contrast vault (172.18.0.13) and seaweedfs-admin (172.18.0.15) are on BOTH bridge+kind and route fine through the edge. Authelia itself is healthy (docker healthcheck green; curl https://127.0.0.1:9091/api/health -> 200).

WHY: scripts/authelia-setup.sh creates the container with '--network bridge' (line 166) and is invoked TWICE from scripts/setup.sh (line 82 and line 921). The single 'docker network connect kind authelia' (setup.sh line 552, guarded by '2>/dev/null || true') runs BETWEEN the two invocations, so the late re-run at 921 recreates the container bridge-only and drops the kind attachment; nothing reconnects it afterward.

FIX OPTIONS: (a) move/duplicate the 'network connect kind authelia' to AFTER the final authelia-setup.sh at setup.sh:921; or (b) attach kind inside authelia-setup.sh right after container creation; or (c) make authelia-setup.sh idempotent so the 921 run doesn't recreate the container. Remove the error-swallowing '2>/dev/null || true' or at least log a warning so this fails loudly.

VERIFY AFTER FIX: docker inspect authelia shows both bridge+kind; curl -sk https://authelia.172-18-0-250.sslip.io/api/health -> 200; curl -sk https://authelia.172-18-255-200.sslip.io/.well-known/openid-configuration -> issuer==in-cluster host; seaweedfs-admin unauth -> 302 to authelia (not 500).

BLOCKS: cnpg-playground-1xa (its live in-cluster-portal + OIDC-issuer verification cannot pass while authelia is unreachable).
close_reason: Fixed + clean-recreate validated 2026-07-02. authelia-setup.sh now attaches authelia to the kind network right after (re)create; a full teardown+setup left authelia on 'bridge kind' with no hot-fix, edge /api/health 200, forward-auth allow/deny correct via Playwright. Root cause (bridge-only recreate) permanently resolved at source.

title: monitoring/setup.sh: fresh-cluster deadlock — otel-collector helm --wait blocks on otlp-tls secret created only after install
description: On teardown+recreate, ./monitoring/setup.sh fails at the otel-collector helm install ('Progress deadline exceeded' x3, exit 1). Root cause: otel-collector-values.yaml mounts secret otel-collector-otlp-tls as a REQUIRED volume, and helm_upgrade_install uses --wait, but the cert-manager Certificate that issues that secret (monitoring/platform/ext-svc-lb.yaml) is applied AFTER the helm install. Fresh clusters have no pre-existing secret, so the pod is stuck ContainerCreating, helm --wait times out, and the script dies before ever applying the cert -> unrecoverable. Worked previously only because the secret already existed from a prior run. Introduced by 5sq.6 (edge->collector OTLP mTLS).

title: traefik-edge crash-loops: OTLP mTLS client cert never generated
description:
Symptom surfaced as vault-oidc-setup.sh failing at setup.sh:845 ('error checking oidc discovery URL', PUT auth/oidc/config, 400). Real cause: traefik-edge was crash-looping (ExitCode 1, no IP), so nothing listened on 172.18.0.250:443 and Vault could not reach https://authelia.<edge>.sslip.io/.well-known/openid-configuration.

Root cause: traefik-edge/traefik.yaml references /etc/traefik/certs/otlp-client.crt + .key in 3 places (tracing, log, accessLog OTLP mTLS), but the keypair was never generated. traefik-edge-setup.sh:98 only had a COMMENT claiming it is 'provisioned in cnpg-playground-5sq.6' (monitoring/setup.sh). But per setup.sh ordering the edge starts at line 556 while monitoring/setup.sh runs at line 1257 (~700 lines / entire core bootstrap later) -> the cert would never exist when the edge first starts. Traefik v3.7 fatals loading the missing keypair. The crash is SILENT because the edge's app-log output (log.otlp) is OTLP-only with no stdout fallback -> 'docker logs traefik-edge' is empty.

Fix (applied, scripts/traefik-edge-setup.sh): issue the cert via the existing _issue_cert helper (step-ca x5c) before the edge starts: _issue_cert otlp-client traefik-edge.<edge>.sslip.io traefik-edge localhost 127.0.0.1. Removed the misleading 5sq.6 comment.

Cross-script coordination verified: collector OTLP receiver client_ca_file = step-ca-external-bundle (<- step-ca-roots, the step-ca root); the otlp-client cert is step-ca-x5c-issued full-chain -> accepted. monitoring/setup.sh needs no change. scripts/setup.sh edge start (556) now has the cert present.

Verified live: re-ran traefik-edge-setup.sh -> otlp-client.crt/key created; docker restart traefik-edge -> Up, IP 172.18.0.250 assigned; curl https://authelia.<edge>.sslip.io/.well-known/openid-configuration -> HTTP 200 (Vault's failing URL now works).
close_reason: Fixed in scripts/traefik-edge-setup.sh: issue otlp-client cert via step-ca before the edge starts. Verified live: edge Up, IP assigned, Authelia discovery through edge returns 200.

title: In-cluster Traefik values break on chart v41: logs->log/accessLog rename
description:
helm install of in-cluster Traefik (chart 41.0.1) failed schema validation: "additional properties 'logs' not allowed", aborting setup.sh at line 727. traefik-helm-chart v41.0.0 (2026-06-16) is a breaking change aligning log keys with upstream Traefik syntax (PR #1887): logs.general -> log, logs.access -> accessLog, field/filter keys camelCased (defaultmode -> defaultMode, statuscodes -> statusCodes, etc.), and the fields.general nesting level removed (fields.general.defaultmode -> fields.defaultMode). accessLog.enabled toggle retained.

Fix (applied, traefik/values.yaml): migrated the logs: block to v41 log:/accessLog: syntax with camelCased fields and flattened fields.general. accessLog.enabled: true kept. Repo does not use providers.file.content (the other v41 breaking change), so unaffected. Verified: 'helm template ... --version 41.0.1 -f traefik/values.yaml' renders and emits --accesslog=true + all fields.
close_reason: Fixed in traefik/values.yaml: migrated logs: -> log:/accessLog: for chart v41 breaking rename. Verified via helm template render.

title: Authelia readiness probe fails: OIDC discovery rejects loopback issuer
description:
authelia-setup.sh readiness poll hit https://127.0.0.1:9091/.well-known/openid-configuration. Authelia 4.39 derives the effective OIDC issuer per request and refuses discovery unless the issuer URL falls under a configured session.cookies domain (the only domain is ${TRAEFIK_EDGE_IP_DASHED}.sslip.io). 127.0.0.1 has no matching cookie domain -> 400 'no session cookie configuration matches url' on every retry -> setup aborts. Container itself is healthy ('Startup complete', listening on :9091); only the probe failed. Regression from 728fc3e (5sq.4 OIDC re-bootstrap) which moved the issuer to the edge and made discovery host-sensitive.

Root cause detail: even hitting the edge hostname directly keeps the non-standard :9091 on the Host, so the derived issuer https://authelia.<edge>.sslip.io:9091 still misses the port-less cookie domain. Confirmed via deepwiki (GetCookieConfigFromAutheliaURL) + live repro.

Fix (applied, scripts/authelia-setup.sh): poll the discovery endpoint via --resolve <edge-host>:9091:127.0.0.1 with X-Forwarded-Proto/Host (no port) headers, replicating how the edge Traefik calls Authelia. Derived issuer becomes port-less https://authelia.<edge>.sslip.io -> matches cookie domain -> 200. Self-contained (does not depend on the edge being deployed yet). Verified against the live failed-run container: probe now exits 0.
close_reason: Fixed in scripts/authelia-setup.sh: readiness probe now uses --resolve + X-Forwarded-Host (port-less) so derived OIDC issuer matches the session cookie domain. Verified passing against live container.

title: self-service-setup.sh: Vault DB static-role rotation fails — vde_config lacks ADMIN OPTION on app role (PG16+)
description:
After the Pooler fix (cnpg-playground-uwm), demo/self-service-setup.sh setup local now fails later (exit 2) at the Vault Database Secrets Engine step: 'vault write database/static-roles/app' returns Code 500: error setting credentials: failed to execute query: ERROR: permission denied to alter role (SQLSTATE 42501).

Root cause: cluster is PostgreSQL 18 (ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18-standard-trixie). In PG16+, a role with CREATEROLE may only ALTER roles it holds ADMIN OPTION on. rbr_ver_vde_config (the Vault DB config user) is created WITH CREATEROLE and granted ADMIN OPTION on rbr_ver_ddl_{owner,admin,reader} only. The Vault static role rotates the CNPG-managed 'app' login role via 'ALTER ROLE "app" WITH PASSWORD ...', but app/readonly are created by CNPG (superuser), so vde_config has no admin over them. Verified live: pg_auth_members shows vde_config admin_option=t on the 3 ddl roles, absent for app/readonly; rolcreaterole=t, rolsuper=f.

Fix: in the psql_primary block that creates rbr_ver_vde_config, add 'GRANT "app" TO rbr_ver_vde_config WITH ADMIN OPTION;' and the same for readonly. These run after the cluster is ready, so the CNPG managed roles already exist. File: demo/self-service-setup.sh (~line 388).
acceptance_criteria: ./demo/self-service-setup.sh setup local completes exit 0 through the Vault DB Secrets Engine step; vault read database/static-creds/app returns a rotated password.
close_reason: Fixed + verified live. GRANT app/readonly TO vde_config WITH ADMIN OPTION (commit 74d7004). ESO verstappen-app ExternalSecret (reads database/static-creds/app) is SecretSynced/Ready=True → Vault static-role rotation of app succeeds. AC met.

title: self-service-setup.sh: Pooler 'pooler-verstappen-rw' fails admission — spec.template.spec.containers required
description:
demo/self-service-setup.sh setup local aborts (exit 1) at line 332 (kubectl apply of cluster-verstappen.yaml.tpl). The Cluster/ScheduledBackup apply but the Pooler is rejected: 'The Pooler "pooler-verstappen-rw" is invalid: spec.template.spec.containers: Required value'.

Root cause: Workstream J added spec.template.spec to the Pooler to pin PgBouncer to the app node pool (nodeSelector + preferred podAntiAffinity). The Pooler CRD (postgresql.cnpg.io/v1, operator cloudnative-pg v1.29.0) embeds a core PodSpec whose structural schema marks 'containers' as required. Setting any template.spec without a containers entry fails admission. Verified against live CRD: spec.template.spec.required=[containers]; container items.required=[name].

Fix: add a stub container 'name: pgbouncer' under template.spec.containers — CNPG overlays the real image/command/config onto the pgbouncer-named container. Verified via kubectl apply --dry-run=server: pooler now 'created'. File: demo/yaml/self-service/rbr-ver-db/cluster-verstappen.yaml.tpl.
acceptance_criteria: ./demo/self-service-setup.sh setup local completes exit 0; pooler-verstappen-rw pods schedule onto app nodes; PgBouncer reachable.
close_reason: Fixed + verified live (kind-k8s-local). Stub pgbouncer container added to Pooler template (commit 276ebf4); pooler-verstappen-rw 2/2 Running on app nodes (worker3/worker4). AC met: setup completes, pods schedule on app nodes.

title: setup.sh: tenant namespace labeling denied by Capsule webhook (create+patch ordering)
description: setup.sh creates tenant namespaces then PATCHes the capsule.clastix.io/tenant label onto them, which Capsule's namespaces.validating.projectcapsule.dev webhook denies: 'namespace can not be patched into a tenant'. This is by-design hardening (CVE-2024-39690): the tenant label can only be set at namespace CREATE time, not patched onto an existing namespace. Additionally setup.sh applies the Capsule Tenant via ArgoCD root-app AFTER the namespaces, so the Tenant rbr doesn't exist when namespaces are created. Fix: (1) apply the Capsule Tenant directly (kubectl apply manifests/capsule-tenant-rbr.yaml) before namespaces so ArgoCD's prune=false tenant-rbr app adopts it; (2) create namespaces with the capsule.clastix.io/tenant + cnpg.io/driver-group labels in a single CREATE (heredoc apply), not create-then-label. setup.sh runs as cluster-admin which Capsule excludes from tenant enforcement, so CREATE-with-label is accepted. Location: scripts/setup.sh ~line 900-912.
acceptance_criteria: setup.sh completes past tenant namespace creation; rbr-ver and rbr-ver-db exist with capsule.clastix.io/tenant=rbr + cnpg.io/driver-group=ver labels; Tenant rbr status lists both namespaces; ArgoCD tenant-rbr app Synced.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (deeper than first thought): Capsule rejects tenant-namespace creation by anyone who is not a tenant OWNER. Three denial layers observed in sequence: (1) create+patch label -> 'namespace can not be patched into a tenant'; (2) create-with-label as cluster-admin -> 'namespace has tenant label but no Tenant ownerReference' (Capsule's mutating webhook injects the ownerRef only for owners, skips cluster-admin); (3) create-with-label + forged ownerReference as cluster-admin -> 'only tenant owners can create tenant-owned namespaces'. RESOLUTION (validated live via kubectl impersonation): pre-apply Tenant rbr, then create each namespace impersonating the owner group: kubectl --as=capsule-bot --as-group=oidc:rbr-db-admin --as-group=system:authenticated create -f - (NOT apply: capsule-namespace-provisioner ClusterRole grants only create/patch, not get, which apply needs). Capsule auto-injects the Tenant ownerReference; Tenant .status.namespaces shows [rbr-ver, rbr-ver-db]. Added existence-guard for idempotency. ALSO FIXED in same session: common.sh lockfile EXIT-trap referenced an out-of-scope local under set -u (line ~256 'pidfile: unbound variable') -> moved paths to globals.
close_reason: Fixed (Workstream J, already committed) + verified live. Tenant namespaces created via impersonated 'create -f -' (--as=capsule-bot --as-group=oidc:rbr-db-admin). rbr-ver/rbr-ver-db Active with capsule.clastix.io/tenant=rbr + cnpg.io/driver-group=ver; Tenant rbr status lists both; ArgoCD tenant-rbr Synced/Healthy. AC met.

title: gangplank install fails: wrong chart version + nonexistent value keys
description:
setup.sh gangplank install (line ~824) failed during teardown+setup: helm could not find chart 'gangplank' version 0.1.4 in https://peak-scale.github.io/helm-charts (only 0.1.0/0.2.0/0.2.1 are published). Beyond the version, the block was written against a chart schema that does not exist in the SIGHUP gangplank chart (image registry.sighup.io/fury/gangplank):
- oidc.existingSecret / oidc.clientIDKey / oidc.clientSecretKey: no such values; silently ignored, so the gangplank-oidc secret was never consumed and clientID/clientSecret stayed at chart defaults.
- config.groupsClaim: not a valid gangplank config key (config struct has only usernameClaim/emailClaim; group->RBAC mapping happens at the apiserver OIDC layer, not gangplank).
- config.scopes set as a space-delimited string but the field is []string.
- leftover --debug flag.
design: Verified against chart 0.2.1 values + internal/config/config.go. Fix: (1) common.sh GANGPLANK_CHART_VERSION 0.1.4 -> 0.2.1. (2) Rename gangplank-oidc secret keys to env var names GANGPLANK_CONFIG_CLIENT_ID / GANGPLANK_CONFIG_CLIENT_SECRET and inject via --set-json envFrom=[{secretRef:{name:gangplank-oidc}}] (gangplank loads config.yaml then envconfig.Process overrides from GANGPLANK_CONFIG_* env). (3) Drop oidc.* and config.groupsClaim. (4) config.scopes via --set-json as a JSON list. (5) remove --debug. Validated with helm template: renders clean, scopes is a list, both secretRefs present.
acceptance_criteria: teardown+setup completes past the gangplank install; gangplank pod reaches Ready; config.yaml in the gangplank configmap is valid and client creds come from the gangplank-oidc secret.
close_reason: Fixed: chart 0.1.4->0.2.1, dropped nonexistent oidc.*/groupsClaim keys, scopes as JSON list, creds via GANGPLANK_CONFIG_* envFrom secret, removed --debug. Validated live: gangplank 1/1 Running, scopes list correct, creds injected from gangplank-oidc secret.

title: Capsule 0.7.3 helm install hangs on K8s 1.35 (context canceled)
description:
## What
helm_upgrade_install capsule oci://ghcr.io/projectcapsule/charts/capsule 0.7.3 hangs and eventually gets killed with 'context canceled' on every attempt (3-retry loop all fail).

## Evidence
setup.sh log shows:
  Pulled: ghcr.io/projectcapsule/charts/capsule:0.7.3
  Release capsule has been cancelled.
  Error: context canceled

## Why it likely fails
0.7.3 is 6 minor releases behind 0.13.6 (latest). Capsule 0.x shipped with admission webhooks that depend on API versions likely deprecated or removed in K8s 1.35.0. The helm --wait flag then blocks forever waiting for pods that never become Ready.

## Acceptance
Capsule installs successfully in kind k8s-local and helm status shows deployed.
notes:
RESOLVED & validated live on K8s 1.35 kind cluster. Root causes were a chain of 4 issues:
1. Chart version: 0.7.3 (capsule-proxy 0.7.3 didn't exist in OCI registry) -> bumped to capsule 0.13.6 / capsule-proxy 0.13.5 (common.sh).
2. 'context canceled': OS 'timeout 360s' killed helm mid CRD-lifecycle ConfigMap dance (Capsule 0.13 manages 11 CRDs via sequential delete+wait cycles before the Deployment). Fixed by switching capsule install to --no-wait + explicit 'kubectl rollout status deployment/capsule-controller-manager --timeout=900s' (avoids helm blocking on the CRD dance entirely). OS timeout also raised to 900s, helm --timeout to 800s.
3. capsule-proxy cert issuer name wrong: --set certManager.issuer.name=vault-pki-issuer -> correct ClusterIssuer is 'vault-pki' (NotFound error). Fixed setup.sh:700.
4. capsule-proxy serving cert rejected by Vault: 'role requires keys of type ec'. Vault pki_int role cluster-certs mandates EC keys but the chart defaults to RSA. Added --set certManager.certificate.fields.privateKey.algorithm=ECDSA + size=256 (setup.sh:702-703).

Final validated state: capsule-controller-manager 1/1 Running, capsule-proxy 1/1 Running, capsule-proxy-serving-cert Ready=True (issued by vault-pki, EC key). Both helm releases 'deployed'.
close_reason: Resolved and validated live: capsule + capsule-proxy both deployed and Running on K8s 1.35. Four chained fixes (version bump, --no-wait+rollout-status for the CRD-lifecycle hang, issuer name vault-pki, EC private key for serving cert) all persisted in scripts/common.sh + scripts/setup.sh. See notes for detail.

title: trust-manager Bundle apply races admission webhook (connection refused)
description: After dropping helm --wait for trust-manager, setup.sh line 538-539 applies the step-ca Bundle immediately after 'kubectl wait --for=condition=Available deployment/trust-manager'. The apiserver call to the trust-manager validating webhook fails: dial tcp <clusterIP>:443 connect: connection refused. Root cause (confirmed via k8s MCP): deployment Available reflects the health probe (port 6060) but the webhook server (port 6443) / kube-proxy endpoint programming for the ClusterIP lags, so the webhook isn't reachable at apply time. Pod is healthy and webhook serving seconds later. Fix: retry the Bundle apply until the webhook is reachable (add generic retry helper in common.sh).
notes: Confirmed via k8s MCP: trust-manager pod 1/1 Running, webhook serving on :6443 (log: 'Serving webhook server port=6443' at 21:52:34.636), Service 443->6443, EndpointSlice has ready endpoint. Failure was a timing race: apply fired at the same instant the webhook came up / before kube-proxy programmed the ClusterIP endpoint. Fix: added generic retry() helper in scripts/common.sh; setup.sh renders the step-ca Bundle to a tempfile and applies via 'retry 12 5 kubectl apply' (up to 60s for webhook reachability). Downstream Bundle/ClusterIssuer applies are after this barrier so inherit reachability.

title: demo-app: runtime search_path not applied through PgBouncer (tasks table 'does not exist'); fix via per-connection SET, plus seed wiring
description:
SYMPTOM: After cnpg-playground-bz6, /health/ready (SELECT 1) passed but real table access failed: GET /tasks and POST /tasks/create -> asyncpg UndefinedTableError relation 'tasks' does not exist. Migrations had correctly created dev.tasks and dev.alembic_version.

ROOT CAUSE: The bz6 fix (ignore_startup_parameters: search_path on the Pooler) was INEFFECTIVE. Verified empirically through the live pooler: sending search_path as a startup/options parameter is silently IGNORED by PgBouncer (search_path stayed "$user", public) — ignore_startup_parameters makes PgBouncer accept-and-drop the param, it does NOT apply it. So the app session never had search_path=dev and looked in public, where tasks does not exist. (SELECT 1 worked because it needs no schema.) A plain 'SET search_path TO dev,public' SQL command through the pooler DID work (session pooling), returning the dev tables.

FIX:
1) app/src/demo_app/db/session.py: removed connect_args server_settings search_path; build the engine explicitly and add a SQLAlchemy 'connect' event (pin_search_path helper) that runs 'SET search_path TO "<schema>", public' on every new connection. PgBouncer session pooling preserves it.
2) Reverted the bz6 pooler change: removed ignore_startup_parameters from app/k8s/cluster-demo.yaml.tpl and patched the live pooler (it was a no-op / misleading).

title: demo-app: schema pinned via asyncpg search_path startup param is rejected by PgBouncer pooler (affects prod too)
description:
SYMPTOM: After the dev CrashLoop fix (cnpg-playground-6e2), the app binds :8000 and the startup probe passes, but /health/ready returns 503 on every poll: 'database unavailable: unsupported startup parameter: search_path' (asyncpg.exceptions.ProtocolViolationError). Liveness /health is 200; only DB-touching paths fail.

ROOT CAUSE: src/demo_app/db/session.py:37 pins the schema with connect_args={'server_settings': {'search_path': settings.db_schema}}. asyncpg sends search_path as a Postgres STARTUP parameter. The app connects through the CNPG PgBouncer pooler (database.host = pooler-demo-rw.demo-db.svc.cluster.local), and PgBouncer rejects any startup parameter not in its allow-list. Migrations are unaffected because they bypass the pooler via migrationHost (demo-rw, the -rw service). This is LATENT IN PROD TOO: prod sends search_path=public the same way through the pooler; it only surfaced now because dev was exercised end-to-end.

FIX APPLIED: added ignore_startup_parameters: 'search_path' to the Pooler's pgbouncer.parameters in app/k8s/cluster-demo.yaml.tpl, and patched the live Pooler pooler-demo-rw in demo-db. Verified via cloudnative-pg source (deepwiki): PgBouncer still forwards search_path to PostgreSQL (wildcard '*' db relays connection params), so schema selection is preserved; pool mode is 'session' so it persists per session. CNPG reloads pgbouncer.ini via RELOAD (no pooler pod restart). RESULT: /health/ready now 200, app pod ready, 0 restarts.

FOLLOW-UP / ALTERNATIVE (not done): a pooler-agnostic app-side fix would set search_path via a per-connection 'SET search_path TO <schema>, public' (SQLAlchemy connect event) instead of an asyncpg startup parameter — more portable and safe under transaction-mode pooling. Current fix is the canonical CNPG approach and is sufficient given session pooling.

NOTE: ensure the prod cluster/pooler (if/when deployed via setup.sh --with-app) also gets this Pooler param — the tpl change covers it, but any already-running prod pooler needs the same patch.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: dev app binds :8000, startup+readiness probes pass, 0 restarts

title: demo-app dev (Tilt) CrashLoopBackOff: --reload worker OOM-killed under 128Mi limit, never binds :8000
description:
SYMPTOM: In Tilt/dev (namespace demo-dev), demo-app is in CrashLoopBackOff. Startup probe GET http://POD:8000/health/startup fails with 'connection refused' for the full 30x2s=60s budget, then kubelet kills the container ('Container app failed startup probe, will be restarted'). Logs stop after uvicorn prints 'Will watch for changes in these directories: [/app]' — the worker never reaches 'Uvicorn running on 0.0.0.0:8000', so nothing ever binds 8000.

ROOT CAUSE: The dev command (migration.strategy=startup) is sh -c 'litestar db upgrade --no-prompt && litestar run ... --reload'. --reload forks a SECOND full Python interpreter (litestar[standard] + advanced-alchemy + otel instrumentation). values-dev.yaml sets the dev memory limit to 128Mi (HALF of prod's 256Mi) and cpu 250m. The reload worker child is OOM-killed by the cgroup before it binds the socket. Because the OOM victim is a child process (not PID 1 = sh), the container is NOT reported as OOMKilled — instead it just never listens and is killed for failing the startup probe, looking like a slow/hung start. Compounding: --reload watches /app, which contains 7026 of 7108 files in /app/.venv, adding needless memory/CPU/inotify pressure to the initial scan.

NOT THE CAUSE: /health/startup endpoint is correct (controllers/health.py:28-31 returns 200 {status: started}); probe path/port match. DB upgrade succeeds (migrations 001,002 apply). Prod path (initContainer migration, no --reload, 256Mi) works fine.

FIX (in priority order):
1) PRIMARY: raise dev memory limit to >=256Mi in app/helm/demo-app/values-dev.yaml (reload needs two interpreters; 128Mi is below prod).
2) Restrict reload watch to source: 'litestar run --reload --reload-dir src' so it does not watch ~7000 .venv files. Edit the startup command in app/helm/demo-app/templates/deployment.yaml (and the --reload branch). Cuts memory+CPU+inotify.
3) OPTIONAL: widen startup probe budget for the startup-migration strategy (db upgrade + worker spawn under 250m cpu is tight) — bump startupProbe.failureThreshold or add initialDelaySeconds in deployment.yaml.
4) DEBUG LOGGING: values-dev already sets logLevel: DEBUG + debug: true, plumbed via configmap DEMO_APP_LOG_LEVEL -> settings.log_level -> structlog (main.py:89-95). It produces no output only because the worker dies before app init. Optionally add '--log-level debug' to the litestar run command so uvicorn/reloader detail surfaces, but this is not the root cause.

EVIDENCE: pod demo-app-* in demo-dev, RESTARTS climbing, events show repeated 'Startup probe failed ... connection refused' then 'failed startup probe, will be restarted'; previous-container logs end at 'Will watch for changes ... [/app]'; exec confirmed 0 listeners on 8000 and 7026 files under /app/.venv.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: dev app binds :8000, startup+readiness probes pass, 0 restarts

title: fix(calico): docker hub 429 rate limit on calico image pulls in Kind
description:
All calico pods (calico-node, calico-kube-controllers, calico-apiserver) enter ImagePullBackOff because Kind nodes hit Docker Hub's anonymous pull rate limit (HTTP 429 Too Many Requests).

Root cause: 7 Kind nodes all pulling docker.io/calico/* images simultaneously from the same host IP exhausts the anonymous pull quota (100 pulls / 6h / IP).

Affected images:
- docker.io/calico/node:v3.29.1
- docker.io/calico/kube-controllers:v3.29.1
- docker.io/calico/apiserver:v3.29.1

Fix options (preferred first):
1. Pre-pull images on host + kind load docker-image before helm install — avoids all registry traffic from nodes
2. Authenticate Kind nodes to Docker Hub via imagePullSecret
3. Mirror images to a local registry and patch the Installation CR imagePrefix

Option 1 is simplest for this playground: docker pull each image, then kind load docker-image <image> --name k8s-local for each, before running helm install tigera-operator.
close_reason: Fixed: preload_images_into_kind() in common.sh + call in setup.sh before Calico install. All docker.io images pulled on host and kind-loaded before cluster deployment.

But kubectl get pod exits 0 even when the namespace exists and there are NO matching pods (it just prints 'No resources found'). So the loop exits immediately after calico-system is created, before any pods are scheduled, and then kubectl wait fails with 'error: no matching resources found'. Fix: pipe the output through a grep or --no-headers check to confirm at least one pod actually exists.
close_reason: Fixed in scripts/setup.sh — changed until loop to use --no-headers | grep -q . so it only exits when pods actually exist

title: calico bootstrap: two scheduling failures during kind cluster setup
description:
## What happened

Two calico-related failures discovered during Phase 9 setup.sh runs:

**Bug 1 — kubectl wait race (fixed ab4f621 never ran, was 4fb5633):**
`kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod -l k8s-app=calico-node` ran immediately after `kubectl apply` of the Installation CR, before the operator had a chance to create the calico-system namespace + calico-node DaemonSet. Exit: `error: no matching resources found`.
Fix: added `until kubectl get pod ... &>/dev/null` poll loop before the wait.

**Bug 2 — values file dropped chart defaults (fixed ab4f621):**
`k8s/calico/tigera-operator-values.yaml` overrode `tolerations` with only the control-plane toleration, removing the chart defaults (`operator: Exists` for NoExecute+NoSchedule). During bootstrap, Kubernetes adds `node.kubernetes.io/not-ready:NoSchedule` to all nodes (no CNI → all NotReady). Without catch-all tolerations, 0/7 nodes were schedulable.
Also overrode `nodeSelector` without preserving the required `kubernetes.io/os: linux` default.
Fix: restored full default tolerations + os nodeSelector, added control-plane label on top.

## Acceptance criteria
- `./scripts/setup.sh local` completes without calico-related scheduling or wait errors
- tigera-operator pod lands on control-plane node
- calico-node DaemonSet rolls out on all non-postgres nodes
close_reason: Both fixes validated: setup.sh completes successfully

title: Authelia: blank login page + unwanted 2FA prompt
description:
Two related issues with the Authelia login interface.

## Issue 1: Blank page on login

### Root Causes

**Session cookie domain mismatch (primary cause)**
Authelia session is configured for domain 172-31-175-83.sslip.io only. When the frontend loads from localhost, the SPA calls /api/state which returns: 'unable to retrieve session cookie domain provider: no configured session cookie domain matches https://localhost:9091/api/state'. SPA cannot determine auth state → blank page.

**TLS: unknown certificate authority**
Browser rejects TLS handshake (cert hostname != localhost, internal CA not trusted by browser). Log: 'remote error: tls: unknown certificate authority'

**admin user missing from users_database.yml**
users_database.yml.tpl defines admin user but the generated users_database.yml only has: dexuser, rbr-admin, rbr-ver-admin, unrelated. Admin login fails even with the correct URL.

**YAML syntax bug in users_database.yml.tpl**
Line reads: email:admin@example.com (missing space after colon). Should be: email: admin@example.com. Would break admin user loading on regeneration.

### Immediate Workaround
Access via https://authelia.172-31-175-83.sslip.io:9091 (must also trust internal CA or accept TLS warning).

## Issue 2: 2FA required, should be 1FA

The Authelia portal itself (login page) is prompting for 2-factor auth. Only 1-factor (password) should be required for the Authelia interface.

Current config has default_policy: one_factor with no access_control rules, so 2FA may be triggered by a previously registered TOTP device on the user account, or by a misconfiguration.

Fix: verify no user has a registered 2FA device that forces elevation, and ensure access_control rules do not require two_factor for the Authelia portal domain.

## Files
- authelia/config/configuration.yaml (session domain, access_control)
- authelia/config/users_database.yml (missing admin user)
- authelia/config/users_database.yml.tpl (YAML bug: email:admin@example.com)
notes: Fixed: admin user added to users_database.yml and .tpl (commit 08cb03e). 2FA prompt was browser localStorage caching an old forwardAuth target — cleared by wiping site data. Root access_control config (default_policy: one_factor) was already correct. No TOTP devices registered, no server-side fix needed.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bug: Authelia 4.38 config schema errors — claims_policies and deprecated userinfo key
description:
Authelia 4.38.19 rejects configuration with two classes of errors:

1. FATAL — unknown keys (config written for wrong schema version):
   - identity_providers.oidc.claims_policies.default_policy.id_token
   - identity_providers.oidc.claims_policies.default_policy.id_token[].name
   - identity_providers.oidc.clients[].claims_policy

2. WARNING (auto-mapped, not fatal — but noisy):
   - userinfo_signing_algorithm deprecated, replaced by userinfo_signed_response_alg

The claims_policies block and claims_policy client reference are either:
  a) Not yet in 4.38 (introduced in a later version), or
  b) Using the wrong key names for 4.38

Need to investigate the correct Authelia 4.38 schema for custom claims/scopes in OIDC clients.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE: claims_policies, id_token array, and clients[].claims_policy are Authelia 4.39.0 features — not available in 4.38.19 (confirmed via DeepWiki). These were written against a schema from a later version. Also: userinfo_signing_algorithm was renamed to userinfo_signed_response_alg in 4.38.0.

EVIDENCE: Authelia 4.38.19 errors:
  - 'configuration key not expected: claims_policies.default_policy.id_token' → 4.39 feature
  - 'configuration key not expected: clients[].claims_policy' → 4.39 feature

title: Bug: Authelia config YAML fails — template engine not enabled (X_AUTHELIA_CONFIG_FILTERS missing)
description:
Authelia fails to start with 'yaml: invalid map key' because the configuration template engine is not enabled. The config file uses Authelia's Go template syntax ({{ secret "/config/secrets/jwks_rsa_private.pem" | mindent 10 "|" | msquote }}) for the OIDC JWKS key, but the template engine must be explicitly enabled — it does NOT run automatically.

Symptoms in docker logs:
  level=error msg="Configuration: failed to load configuration from file path(/config/configuration.yml) source: yaml: invalid map key: map[string]interface {}{"secret "/config/secrets/jwks_rsa_private.pem" | mindent 10 "|" | msquote"...}"
  (followed by cascading validation errors for all config sections)
  level=fatal msg="Can't continue due to the errors loading the configuration"

Root cause (via DeepWiki): Authelia's template filter is not run unless explicitly enabled via:
  - Env var: X_AUTHELIA_CONFIG_FILTERS=template
  - CLI flag: --config.experimental.filters template

Fix: add -e X_AUTHELIA_CONFIG_FILTERS=template to the docker run command in authelia-setup.sh.

Note: the 'Exited (0)' from Bug c07 masked this issue previously; now that c07 is fixed and Authelia finds the config, this YAML error surfaces.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via DeepWiki): Authelia's Go template filter (which processes {{ secret ... | mindent | msquote }} expressions) is NOT enabled by default. It must be explicitly activated.

The config file uses Authelia's template functions for the OIDC JWKS key:
  key: {{ secret "/config/secrets/jwks_rsa_private.pem" | mindent 10 "|" | msquote }}

Without the filter, YAML parser sees raw {{ }} as a flow mapping, producing:
  yaml: invalid map key: map[string]interface {}{"secret ...": nil}
All subsequent config sections then fail validation (cascading errors).

FIX APPLIED (authelia-setup.sh): Added -e X_AUTHELIA_CONFIG_FILTERS=template to docker run.
  BEFORE: docker run -d --network bridge ...
  AFTER:  docker run -d --network bridge -e X_AUTHELIA_CONFIG_FILTERS=template ...

SEQUENCE: c07 (.yaml→.yml) → Authelia finds config → bg3 (template not enabled) → Authelia parses config. Both fixes required.
close_reason: Fixed in authelia-setup.sh: added -e X_AUTHELIA_CONFIG_FILTERS=template to docker run so Authelia processes {{ secret ... | mindent | msquote }} before YAML parsing.

title: Bug: Authelia exits immediately — config mounted as .yaml but entrypoint expects .yml
description:
Authelia container (4.38.19) exits with code 0 immediately after startup. Root cause: the docker run command mounts the config at /config/configuration.yaml, but Authelia's entrypoint/binary defaults to looking for /config/configuration.yml. When it does not find configuration.yml, it generates a default config there and exits.

Symptom in docker logs:
  time=... level=warning msg="Configuration did not exist so a default one has been generated at /config/configuration.yml, you will need to configure this"
  Exited (0) 16 seconds ago

Fix: change the volume mount target from /config/configuration.yaml to /config/configuration.yml in authelia-setup.sh:
  -v "${AUTHELIA_CONFIG_DIR}/configuration.yaml:/config/configuration.yml:ro"

Seen during: ./scripts/setup.sh local → authelia-setup.sh phase → 'Authelia did not become ready'
notes:
ROOT CAUSE: authelia-setup.sh mounted config at /config/configuration.yaml:ro but Authelia's ConfigEnsureExistsRunE looks for /config/configuration.yml (default path). When .yml not found, it generates a default and calls os.Exit(0) — hence 'Exited (0) 16 seconds' and the warning message.

EVIDENCE: docker logs show structured Authelia log after chown errors, confirming the binary ran but exited via ConfigEnsureExistsRunE. DeepWiki confirmed: if --config is not explicitly passed, Authelia defaults to /config/configuration.yml; if missing, generates default and exits 0.

FIX APPLIED (authelia-setup.sh): Changed volume mount target from /config/configuration.yaml to /config/configuration.yml:
  BEFORE: -v "${AUTHELIA_CONFIG_DIR}/configuration.yaml:/config/configuration.yaml:ro"
  AFTER:  -v "${AUTHELIA_CONFIG_DIR}/configuration.yaml:/config/configuration.yml:ro"

ALTERNATIVE (not applied): pass -- --config /config/configuration.yaml after the image name, which would also suppress ConfigEnsureExistsRunE.
close_reason: Fixed in authelia-setup.sh: changed volume mount target from /config/configuration.yaml to /config/configuration.yml so Authelia's ConfigEnsureExistsRunE finds the config and starts normally instead of generating a default and exiting.

title: Bug: loki-bucket-init fails silently — mc alias set error suppressed
description: loki-bucket-init pod is in Error state (exit 1) with zero log output. The mc alias set command has >/dev/null 2>&1 which hides the actual failure reason. Pod uses credentials loki/lokiS3secret against https://seaweedfs:8333. k8s Service seaweedfs ClusterIP exists on 8333. Root cause unknown — could be wrong credentials, cert issue, or connectivity.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE: Two layered issues.
1. SeaweedFS main container -ip.bind was missing so it only bound to the bridge interface (172.17.x.x), not the kind network IP. Fixed by adding -ip.bind=0.0.0.0 to the docker run command.
2. TLS key file at seaweedfs/tls/seaweedfs_key.pem had chmod 640 root:root but the weed process runs as seaweed (UID 1000), making the key unreadable and silently preventing TLS from starting. Fixed by chmod 600 + setfacl -m u:1000:r (matching the RustFS pattern).
3. loki identity in identities.json lacked Admin action, so mc mb (CreateBucket) was denied. Adding Admin to the loki identity allows both bucket creation and auto-create-on-first-write.

FIX: scripts/setup.sh updated with all three fixes. identities.json updated at runtime. After restart, loki S3 HTTPS (port 8333) TLS handshake completes and bucket creation works.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bug: SeaweedFS admin UI timeout — HTTPS not responding on port 23646
description: Admin container logs show TLS starting on port 23646, but HTTPS connections time out (curl returns 000). HTTP returns 400 instantly. netstat inside container shows only TCP 23646 (HTTP) and 33646 (gRPC) — no separate TLS listener. Certs exist at /etc/seaweedfs/tls/. Root cause unclear: TLS may not be binding despite log message, or cert has a handshake issue.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE: TLS key file at seaweedfs/tls/seaweedfs_key.pem had chmod 640 root:root but seaweedfs-admin runs as seaweed (UID 1000). Key unreadable → TLS silently not initialized → port 23646 served plain HTTP only → browser/curl timeout when expecting HTTPS.
Also: cert SAN was missing DNS:localhost and IP:127.0.0.1 (needed when accessing admin via localhost in browser). setup.sh was already updated for this SAN.

FIX: chmod 600 + setfacl -m u:1000:r on key file (matching RustFS pattern). setfacl also applied to the tls directory for traversal. After docker restart seaweedfs-admin, TLS initialized successfully. curl -k https://localhost:23646 returns 200. setup.sh updated to apply setfacl on every cert regeneration.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add weed admin container with TLS alongside weed server
description: weed admin is a standalone process (separate from weed server) that connects to the master and provides the web admin UI. TLS for admin requires security.toml with [https.admin] cert/key. Need to: (1) generate security.toml after TLS cert provisioning, (2) start seaweedfs-admin container connecting to seaweedfs master, (3) expose port 23646. Add SEAWEEDFS_ADMIN_CONTAINER_NAME and SEAWEEDFS_ADMIN_PORT back to common.sh.

Generate security.toml with cert/key pointing to the same SeaweedFS TLS cert (SAN includes seaweedfs hostname). Start seaweedfs-admin container on bridge network connecting to master via bridge IP. Port 23646 mapped on host. common.sh: restored SEAWEEDFS_ADMIN_PORT + added SEAWEEDFS_ADMIN_CONTAINER_NAME. setup.sh: generate security.toml + start seaweedfs-admin after TLS restart.

title: Bug: loki-bucket-init still times out — SeaweedFS weed mini TLS/HTTPS not binding on port 8333
description: After switching to weed mini + -s3.port=0 + -s3.port.https=8333, loki-bucket-init pod still times out. The mc --insecure alias set https://seaweedfs:8333 command is failing. Root cause unknown — needs investigation of SeaweedFS container logs and whether -s3.port.https is a valid flag for weed mini (vs weed server -s3).
notes: Both issues resolved by switching to weed server -filer -s3. weed mini had internal health check probing disabled HTTP port (port 0) causing false S3 failure, and likely also had a bug where -s3.port.https=8333 didn't properly initialize the TLS listener (log said 'https port 8333' but handshake timed out). weed server -s3 uses the production-tested TLS code path (same as standalone weed s3 command). HTTP S3 moved to port 8334 to avoid conflict and give health checks a valid endpoint.
close_reason: Root cause: weed mini has internal health check bug probing disabled HTTP port (port 0), and likely fails to properly bind TLS on HTTPS port despite log claiming 'https port 8333'. Fix: weed server -filer -s3 uses production-tested TLS code path. Both HTTP+HTTPS S3 now run on separate ports (8334 HTTP, 8333 HTTPS).

title: Bug: helm_upgrade_install fails with GitHub CDN 504 on chart downloads — no retry
description: setup.sh consistently fails on MetalLB (and previously CNPG) chart downloads with '504 Gateway Time-out' from GitHub. The helm_upgrade_install helper has no retry logic so a single transient CDN failure aborts the entire setup. Fix: wrap the helm upgrade --install call with a retry loop (3 attempts, 15s back-off) in helm_upgrade_install in scripts/common.sh.
notes: Fix: added 3-attempt retry loop with 15s back-off in helm_upgrade_install in scripts/common.sh. On helm failure, prints '⚠️ attempt N/3 failed, retrying in 15s' and retries. After 3 failures, prints error and returns 1. Covers GitHub CDN 504 and similar transient fetch errors.

title: Bug: SeaweedFS filer port 8888 conflicts with existing host service

title: Bug: loki-bucket-init still times out — HTTP/HTTPS port conflict on SeaweedFS S3 port 8333
description: loki-bucket-init pod times out even at 180s. Root cause: scripts/setup.sh runs SeaweedFS with '-s3.port.https=8333' but does not disable the default HTTP S3 port (also 8333). This port conflict prevents SeaweedFS from binding HTTPS correctly, causing 'mc --insecure alias set https://seaweedfs:8333' to hang/fail. Fix: switch to 'weed mini' and add '-s3.port=0' to disable HTTP S3 so only HTTPS S3 runs on 8333.
notes: Root cause confirmed: -s3.port.https=8333 + default -s3.port=8333 (HTTP) on same port prevented HTTPS from binding. mc --insecure alias set https://seaweedfs:8333 hung because no listener responded. Fix: switched to 'weed mini' + added -s3.port=0 to disable HTTP S3. Port conflict resolved.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bug: revocation exporter manifests reference non-existent 'monitoring' namespace
description:
setup.sh fails with:
  Error from server (NotFound): error when creating "STDIN": namespaces "monitoring" not found

The revocation exporter k8s manifests (service.yaml.tpl, servicemonitor.yaml, prometheusrule.yaml) all hardcode 'namespace: monitoring', but this cluster deploys the monitoring stack into the 'prometheus-operator' namespace. The 'monitoring' namespace is never created.

Prometheus CR uses empty selectors (serviceMonitorNamespaceSelector: {}, ruleNamespaceSelector: {}) so it watches all namespaces — the ServiceMonitor and PrometheusRule will be picked up from any namespace.

Fix: change 'namespace: monitoring' to 'namespace: prometheus-operator' in all three revocation exporter manifests.
close_reason: Changed namespace: monitoring → namespace: prometheus-operator in service.yaml.tpl, servicemonitor.yaml, and prometheusrule.yaml. Prometheus CR watches all namespaces so the ServiceMonitor and PrometheusRule are picked up regardless.

title: Bug: tempo-distributed global.extraVolumes not propagated to ingester (StatefulSet) and metricsGenerator pods
description:
After fixing per-component extraVolumeMounts (cnpg-playground-7l7), Helm server-side apply fails with:

  spec.template.spec.containers[0].volumeMounts[3].name: Not found: "step-ca-bundle"

for tempo-ingester (StatefulSet) and tempo-metrics-generator (Deployment).

Root cause: global.extraVolumes in tempo-distributed chart 2.19.0 does NOT propagate the volume to all component pods. It works for some (distributor, compactor, querier, queryFrontend) but not for ingester and metricsGenerator, which appear to use different Helm template paths.

Fix: remove global.extraVolumes and global.extraVolumeMounts entirely; declare both extraVolumes and extraVolumeMounts on every component so each pod is self-contained and no propagation is relied upon.
close_reason: Removed global.extraVolumes/extraVolumeMounts; added both extraVolumes and extraVolumeMounts to all 6 Tempo components (ingester, distributor, compactor, querier, queryFrontend, metricsGenerator). Each pod now declares its own step-ca-bundle volume and mount, bypassing chart propagation inconsistency.

title: Bug: Tempo CA cert volume mounted in pod but not in container — tls_ca_path fails
description:
Tempo pods crash with: 'failed to create TLS config: error loading ca cert: /etc/ssl/step-ca/ca-certificates.crt: open /etc/ssl/step-ca/ca-certificates.crt: no such file or directory'

Root cause: tempo-distributed Helm chart does NOT propagate global.extraVolumeMounts to individual component container specs. The step-ca-bundle volume IS present in the pod's volume list (global.extraVolumes works) but is ABSENT from the container's volumeMounts list. This differs from mimir-distributed where global.extraVolumeMounts correctly reaches container mounts.

Evidence: pod inspection of tempo-compactor shows step-ca-bundle in pod.spec.volumes but not in pod.spec.containers[0].volumeMounts.

Fix: replace tls_ca_path with tls_insecure_skip_verify: true in tempo-values.yaml and remove the now-unused global.extraVolumes/extraVolumeMounts entries. HTTPS is still used (insecure: false) — only cert verification is skipped. Acceptable for a playground with a self-signed step-ca.
close_reason: Added per-component extraVolumeMounts to all 6 Tempo components (ingester, distributor, compactor, querier, queryFrontend, metricsGenerator). The tempo-distributed chart ignores global.extraVolumeMounts for container specs — global.extraVolumes still works for pod-level volume registration. Fix keeps tls_ca_path intact with proper CA verification.

title: Bug: Tempo crashes with 'field http not found in type s3.Config'
description:
All Tempo pods fail to start with YAML parse error:

  failed parsing config: failed to parse configFile /conf/tempo.yaml: yaml: unmarshal errors:
    line 185: field http not found in type s3.Config

Root cause: tempo-values.yaml puts TLS config under a nested 'http:' block inside 'storage.trace.s3', but Tempo 2.10.5's s3.Config struct (tempodb/backend/s3/config.go) inlines tls.ClientConfig from grafana/dskit — TLS fields are directly at the s3 level, not nested under 'http'.

Incorrect (in storage.trace.s3):
  http:
    tls_config:
      ca_cert_path: /etc/ssl/step-ca/ca-certificates.crt

Correct:
  tls_ca_path: /etc/ssl/step-ca/ca-certificates.crt

This was introduced when Phase 4 added TLS to RustFS and the Tempo S3 config was updated to use HTTPS, mistakenly using the same http.tls_config nesting that was applied to Mimir (which also turned out to be wrong for a different reason).
close_reason: Fixed: Removed http sub-block from storage.trace.s3 in tempo-values.yaml. Tempo 2.10.5 s3.Config inlines tls.ClientConfig from grafana/dskit — tls_ca_path sits directly at the s3 level. Source confirmed at tempodb/backend/s3/config.go: tls.ClientConfig is yaml:",inline".

title: Bug: Mimir crashes with 'field tls_config not found in type common.HTTPConfig'
description:
Mimir 2.16.0 fails to start because mimir-values.yaml uses the wrong S3 TLS config field path.

Error in all Mimir pods:
  error loading config from /etc/mimir/mimir.yaml: Error parsing config file: can't unmarshal common config: key "alertmanager_storage": yaml: unmarshal errors:
    line 29: field tls_config not found in type common.HTTPConfig

Root cause: mimir-values.yaml configures TLS for the RustFS objectstore using the thanos-objstore field naming (http.tls_config.ca_cert_path) but Mimir 2.16.0's s3_storage_backend uses flat fields directly under http: the correct field is http.tls_ca_path.

Incorrect (in common.storage.s3):
  http:
    tls_config:
      ca_cert_path: /etc/ssl/step-ca/ca-certificates.crt

Correct:
  http:
    tls_ca_path: /etc/ssl/step-ca/ca-certificates.crt

This was introduced when Phase 4 added TLS to RustFS and Phase 5 or the monitoring phase wired up Mimir to use HTTPS with the custom CA.
close_reason: Fixed: Mimir 2.16.0 s3_storage_backend uses flat TLS fields under http (tls_ca_path, tls_cert_path, etc) — not a nested tls_config block as in thanos-objstore. Changed http.tls_config.ca_cert_path to http.tls_ca_path in mimir-values.yaml. The nested form caused YAML unmarshal to fail on startup for all Mimir pods.

   - gangplank = SIGHUP/peak-scale OIDC->kubeconfig dispenser (browser-facing UI + OIDC redirect/callback with Authelia); user logs in, downloads a kubeconfig.
   - capsule-proxy = Clastix tenant-scoped Kubernetes API gateway; it is the apiServerURL embedded in the kubeconfig gangplank hands out (config.apiServerURL=https://capsule-proxy...), so tenant kubectl traffic flows THROUGH it for Capsule RBAC filtering.
2. Why it needs to be reachable from outside the cluster (gangplank: human browser + Authelia redirect; capsule-proxy: kubectl client from the host).
3. The correct Traefik exposure for each:
   - gangplank: almost certainly an HTTP IngressRoute on entrypoint 'websecure' (443) to the gangplank Service, with the existing wildcard/Traefik TLS — confirm Service name/port from the peak-scale gangplank chart.
   - capsule-proxy: determine whether it should be an HTTPS IngressRoute (TLS termination at Traefik) or an IngressRouteTCP with TLS passthrough — because it's a Kubernetes API endpoint doing token/cert auth, passthrough may be required so client credentials and TLS SNI reach capsule-proxy intact. Confirm capsule-proxy Service name/port (capsule-system ns) and its TLS mode.
4. Whether the dispensed kubeconfig's server URL (capsule-proxy host) must match a SAN on the serving cert, and how that interacts with sslip.io + the cluster CA.

Deliverable: a short findings note (URL, purpose, chosen Traefik route type + entrypoint + backend Service:port + TLS handling) sufficient to implement the sibling feature bead. Use deepwiki/upstream docs for peak-scale gangplank and clastix capsule-proxy charts; verify Service names against the live cluster (capsule-system, gangplank namespaces).

Research complete → docs/gangplank-capsule-proxy-ingress-research.md.

Findings (verified on live hub cluster):
- gangplank: Service gangplank:80 (plain HTTP) in ns gangplank. Expose via HTTPS IngressRoute on websecure, Traefik-terminated (vault-pki cert) — identical to argocd-server:80 pattern.
- capsule-proxy: Service capsule-proxy:9001 (HTTPS, enableSSL=true) in ns capsule-system. Serving-cert SANs are ONLY [capsule-proxy, capsule-proxy.capsule-system.svc] — NOT the external sslip.io host.

title: Add lockfile/PID guard to setup.sh and teardown.sh
description:
## What
Add a mutual-exclusion lockfile guard to the top of scripts/setup.sh and scripts/teardown.sh (ideally a shared helper in scripts/common.sh) so a second invocation aborts cleanly instead of running concurrently.

## Why
During Capsule debugging, a Capsule install failed mid-flight with 'context "kind-k8s-local" does not exist'. Root cause: the shared kubeconfig (k8s/kube-config.yaml) was truncated to the 28-byte empty skeleton (apiVersion: v1 / kind: Config) by a teardown.sh running concurrently with an in-flight setup.sh. teardown's 'kubectl config delete-context' + 'delete-cluster' emptied the kubeconfig the running helm process depended on. The cluster itself never died — only the kubeconfig was corrupted. This is a concurrency hazard, not a Capsule bug.

## Approach
- Shared helper in common.sh: acquire_lock() using flock on a lockfile (e.g. ${GIT_REPO_ROOT}/.playground.lock) or a PID file with staleness check.
- Call it at the top of setup.sh and teardown.sh after sourcing common.sh.
- On contention: print which PID holds the lock and exit non-zero.
- Release on EXIT via trap (compose with existing _common_on_err ERR trap — use a separate EXIT trap or combine).
- Prefer flock(1) when available (Linux/WSL); guard for macOS where flock may be absent.

## Acceptance
- Running setup.sh while another setup.sh or teardown.sh is active aborts immediately with a clear message and does not touch the kubeconfig or cluster.
- Lock is released on normal exit, error exit, and SIGINT/SIGTERM.
- Stale lock (holder process gone) is detected and reclaimed.
notes: flock approach sketch: exec 9>"${LOCKFILE}"; flock -n 9 || { echo holder=$(cat); exit 1; }. Existing trap is 'trap _common_on_err ERR' in common.sh:32 — don't clobber it; add EXIT/INT/TERM handling separately. Both scripts source common.sh and use shared KUBE_CONFIG_PATH=${GIT_REPO_ROOT}/k8s/kube-config.yaml (common.sh:217).
close_reason: acquire_lock() helper in common.sh using flock on Linux/WSL + PID-file fallback for macOS. Called at top of setup.sh and teardown.sh. EXIT/INT/TERM traps release lock without touching ERR trap.

title: Bug: Authelia entrypoint chown fails on read-only volume mounts
description:
Authelia's entrypoint (/app/entrypoint.sh) tries to chown all config files at startup. All volumes are mounted :ro (configuration.yaml, users_database.yml, tls/, secrets/), so every chown fails with 'Read-only file system'.

Symptoms in docker logs:
  chown: /config/configuration.yaml: Read-only file system
  chown: /config/users_database.yml: Read-only file system
  chown: /config/tls/authelia.key: Read-only file system
  (etc)

The :ro mounts are intentional (security) and ACLs give UID 1000 read access via setfacl, so Authelia should be able to read the files. The chown is unnecessary.

Fix options:
  1. Add --user 1000:1000 to the docker run command so Authelia already runs as the right UID and the entrypoint chown is a no-op (chown to same UID succeeds on :ro)
  2. Investigate whether the chown failure is blocking startup (related to Bug #1 — likely masked by the .yaml/.yml issue)

Note: investigate whether fixing Bug #1 (config filename) resolves this too, or if this needs its own fix.
notes:
INVESTIGATION RESULT: chown failures are cosmetic/non-fatal.

EVIDENCE: Authelia's entrypoint does NOT use set -e, so chown failures do not abort startup. Proof from logs: after all chown errors, the Authelia binary itself ran and produced a structured log entry (ConfigEnsureExistsRunE warning) — meaning execution continued past chown.

The :ro mounts are intentional security hardening. ACLs via setfacl give UID 1000 rwx on all files, so Authelia can read them despite chown not changing ownership.

RESOLUTION: No code change needed. Once Bug c07 (config filename) is fixed, Authelia starts and functions correctly. The chown error lines appear in docker logs but do not affect operation.

If desired to silence the errors: pass --user 1000:1000 in docker run — however on a :ro bind mount chown always fails regardless of the running UID, so this does not help. Only option is to not mount files :ro (not recommended) or accept the cosmetic errors.
close_reason: Won't fix: chown errors on :ro mounts are cosmetic. Entrypoint does not abort on chown failure, and ACLs (setfacl u:1000:rwx) ensure Authelia can read all config files. No operational impact once c07 is fixed.

title: Bug: loki-bucket-init times out — pod-running-timeout too short for cold image pull
description:

  error: timed out waiting for the condition on pods/loki-bucket-init

title: Bug: step ca provisioner update fails with 'too many positional arguments' on step CLI 0.30.2
description:
## What happened
setup.sh fails in Phase 0 (step-ca bootstrap) with:
  too many positional arguments were provided in 'step ca provisioner update <name> [--public-key=<file>]'

Script: scripts/step-ca-setup.sh ~line 279

## Root cause (diagnosed)
step CLI inside smallstep/step-ca:latest is now v0.30.2. The flags used in the script are from an older API:
  - --x509-max-dur=2160h        → unknown flag in 0.30.2
  - --x509-default-dur=720h     → unknown flag in 0.30.2
  - --x509-template-file <path> → renamed to --x509-template=<path> in 0.30.2

When step CLI 0.30.2 encounters the unknown --x509-template-file flag, it stops flag parsing and the value (/home/step/config/leaf-x509-template.json) is treated as a second positional argument, triggering the "too many positional arguments" error.

## What needs to be done
1. Rename --x509-template-file to --x509-template (uses = syntax)
2. Determine how to set x509 max/default duration in step 0.30.2 for JWK provisioner
   - May need to use --x509-min-dur / --x509-default-dur under a different flag name
   - Or set via direct ca.json manipulation
3. Fix scripts/step-ca-setup.sh provisioner update call
4. Validate full setup.sh local run succeeds through Phase 0
notes:
## Root Cause
step CLI in smallstep/step-ca:latest is v0.30.2. The flag --x509-template-file was renamed to --x509-template in this version. When step encounters the unknown flag --x509-template-file, it stops flag parsing and treats the next token (the file path) as a second positional argument, triggering:
  too many positional arguments were provided in 'step ca provisioner update <name> [--public-key=<file>]'

--x509-max-dur and --x509-default-dur are still valid in 0.30.2 (confirmed via --help).

## Fix Applied
scripts/step-ca-setup.sh lines 282 and 296:
  --x509-template-file → --x509-template (two occurrences: JWK update + X5C add)

## Verification
grep -rn 'x509-template-file' scripts/ → 0 matches
close_reason: Fixed: renamed --x509-template-file to --x509-template in scripts/step-ca-setup.sh (lines 282 and 296)
